authors.title: For plugin authors
authors.step2Text: {keygen}, save the key as the {secret} secret, push a tag like {tag}.

authors.api11: API 1.1: every new ability is its own permission (alarms, {tray}, tmgr:// links, web links, statuses, relations, agent work), shown when you install or update. Try them all with {example} in developer mode; the plugin log shows why a call was refused.
authors.api12: API 1.2: plugins can read and write Daily Routines (notes and routines), on this device only — not yet in shared workspaces.
authors.api14: API 1.4: a plugin can show a counter on its own sidebar item. It needs the views:badge permission, shown when you install or update, and no extra consent. Long {tray} titles are shortened with "…" instead of being refused.
authors.api15: API 1.5: plugins can work with pages. pages:read reads and searches them, pages:write creates, edits and appends, and pages:sections lets a plugin write only into its own managed sections. Each is shown when you install or update. Plugins cannot add page types.
authors.api16: API 1.6: a plugin can add up to 3 items to the task … menu, on board cards, in the task list and on the task page. It needs menus:task, which is shown when you install or update. The items appear in their own group while the plugin is running; with more than 4 plugin items in total they move into one Plugins submenu.

accountData.account: {label} name, email address, password hash, the ids of sign-in providers you use (GitHub, Google, Apple, Telegram), your avatar and your settings.
accountData.content: {label} workspaces, tasks, comments, pages, uploaded files, time logs, routines, AI assistant conversations and the work logs of AI agents you connect.
accountData.devices: {label} sign-in sessions, device keys for Face ID sign-in, push tokens of the iOS app, your private notification topic and the access tokens you create for agents and devices.
accountData.alarm: {label} only if you set up alarm calls. It is stored encrypted.
accountData.integrations: {label} your Telegram id and username, data from GitHub repositories you link (including commit author names and emails), and your Cursor API key.
accountData.usage: We use this data to run TMGR for you. We don't store your IP address in the database. Our servers keep client IP addresses in memory for up to an hour to limit abuse such as password guessing.
accountData.title: Data we store for your account

desktopLocal.intro: A local workspace in the desktop app is a database file on your computer, and its backups are saved in a folder on your computer. Its content is not sent to us.
desktopLocal.connects: The desktop app still connects to the internet for a few things:
desktopLocal.updates: It checks GitHub for app updates. GitHub sees your IP address.
desktopLocal.plugins: It refreshes the plugin catalog from GitHub when it starts and every six hours.
desktopLocal.ai: It talks to the AI endpoint you configure yourself, if you set one up.
desktopLocal.usage: It sends usage data only if you turn usage data on (see below).
desktopLocal.noAnalytics: The desktop app never loads Google Analytics or Plausible.
desktopLocal.title: Desktop app without an account

usageData.intro: If you agree, the app sends usage events that are not linked to your account. They show us which screens and guided tours people open and which steps they finish, so we can improve TMGR.
usageData.sent: {label} event names such as {code} with fixed values (for example which tour and which step), a random install id created on your device, a random id for each app start, the app version (major and minor), the platform, whether you use a cloud account or a local workspace, a screen size class (small, medium or large) and the hour of the event.
usageData.neverSent: {label} task, page or comment text, names, emails, file names, workspace names, links, your account id, your sign-in token or cookies.
usageData.ip: {label} is not stored with events. It is held in memory for up to an hour to limit abuse.
usageData.retention: {label} raw events are deleted after 30 days. Daily totals (counts per event, without install ids) are kept for 13 months.
usageData.off: {label} switch off "Share usage data" in Settings → Privacy or below on this page. Sending stops at once in every tab and window, and events waiting on your device are deleted.
usageData.delete: {label} your device keeps a deletion key for each install id. "Delete data already sent" in Settings → Privacy or below on this page uses it to delete those events from our servers, also after you turned sharing off.
usageData.pseudonymous: Because the install id stays the same over time, we treat usage data as pseudonymous personal data. The legal basis is your consent, which you can withdraw at any time.
usageData.title: Usage data (optional)

analytics.title: Google Analytics and page view counts (web)
analytics.google: {ga} is loaded on the web app only after you allow it. It sets cookies ({cookie}) and sends your IP address, device and browser details and the pages you visit to Google. If you decline, it never loads. You can change your choice at any time with "Cookie settings" below or at the bottom of the sign-in page, or in Settings. The legal basis is your consent. See {policy}.
analytics.plausible: {label} the web app counts page views with a Plausible instance that we host ourselves. It sets no cookies and stores no IP addresses or personal identifiers. The desktop app doesn't load it. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in knowing how many people use the site.
analytics.yandex: Yandex Metrica is no longer used.

onboardingAggregates.counts: To see whether onboarding works, we count, across all accounts, how many people signed up, verified their email, created a first task, started a timer, connected an AI agent or finished a guided tour. These numbers come from data TMGR stores anyway. They are only shown as totals, and groups of fewer than 10 people are hidden.
onboardingAggregates.basis: This happens whether or not you share usage data, because it uses account data, not device events. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in improving onboarding. You can object by writing to us (see Contact).
onboardingAggregates.title: Onboarding statistics from account data
